lines.text: So it built a bowl a beetle could believe in.
Big enough to be seen by a brain the size of a pinhead.
Pale enough to glow at dusk like a lamp left on.
And warm — here is the marvel — warm:
the flower burns its own sugars in the mitochondria of its tissue,
thermogenesis, a fever with no infection,
heating the chamber to volatilize the perfume,
to make the bowl a sauna the cold-blooded cannot refuse.
